alerts.title: Carbamazepine–DTG interaction causing viral rebound
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70% and advise using valproic acid instead. Patient started carbamazepine 2 weeks ago and viral load has risen from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence, consistent with reduced DTG exposure from this interaction. The clinician's plan does not address the interaction or consider switching the antiepileptic.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch carbamazepine to valproic acid or another non-interacting antiepileptic, or escalate DTG to twice-daily dosing. Repeat viral load after adjustment.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatraemia
alerts.message: Patient has carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (above therapeutic range 4–12), with nystagmus, ataxia, and tremor on examination, plus hyponatraemia (Na 128 mmol/L) — all consistent with carbamazepine toxicity. The clinician plans dose reduction and repeat level, which is appropriate. Sodium valproate was already in use; guidelines recommend valproic acid as the preferred antiepileptic with DTG. Hyponatraemia may also contribute to neurological symptoms.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, repeat level and sodium. Consider switching to valproate monotherapy to address both toxicity and DTG interaction.

alerts.title: Viral load >50: guideline response not fully addressed
alerts.message: Guidelines require that for VL >50 copies/mL on DTG-based ART, clinicians provide enhanced adherence support, address potential side-effects affecting adherence, and repeat VL in 2–3 months. The clinician attributes the rise to unknown causes but does not document enhanced adherence counselling or a plan to repeat the VL at the appropriate interval. The carbamazepine–DTG interaction is a likely pharmacokinetic cause requiring action beyond adherence support.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, address the carbamazepine–DTG interaction, and repeat viral load in 2–3 months after correcting the interaction.
